render output resolution verification: When verifying Blender render output dimensions, check not only scene.render.resolution_x and resolution_y but also scene.render.resolution_percentage or the effective output size, because Blender can scale final render dimensions by the percentage field.
dependency-chain verification: Avoid separate rule items that only verify static source-file facts, such as a blend object having vertices; they are user-independent and can inflate reward without proving task completion.
large image pixel checks: When expected dimensions may be very large, prefer PIL extrema/histogram or bounded sampling over converting the entire image to a NumPy array to reduce evaluator memory risk.
blend-derived expected values: For robust verification of values derived from a .blend file, prefer invoking `blender --background --python-expr ...` or `blender --background file.blend --python ...` in the expected getter rather than assuming `import bpy` works in system Python.
dependency grounding source files: Do not award task reward for checking immutable source file properties; source grounding checks that are already true initially cause positive initial reward and should be used only to derive expected constants or as non-scoring sanity checks.
vm_command_line blend inspection: When using vm_command_line to inspect a .blend file, the rule judge receives stdout only; parse the emitted JSON and avoid host-side os.path.isfile checks on VM absolute paths such as /home/user/Desktop/file.blend.
blend file verification via command line: When using blender --background to inspect a .blend, include an explicit file-existence/load-path check in the emitted JSON so a missing target file or default scene cannot receive credit.
vm_command_line verification: When using vm_command_line to inspect a .blend file, rule code receives stdout only; do not call os.path.isfile on an absolute VM path inside the judge. Either parse the command output or fetch the file separately with vm_file.
render resolution verification: A robust Blender evaluator can run blender --background on the saved .blend and print JSON from bpy.context.scene.render, then parse stdout from vm_command_line to verify resolution_x, resolution_y, and resolution_percentage.
